Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:10:1.english: Year by year - [This] implies two years. Thirty days in a year are considered a year according to all in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (10b).

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:11:1.english: Completing, yes; giving, no - To give thirty full days, we do not give [them].

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:12:1.hebrew: והראה מומו - לאחר שחיטה, ונמצא קבוע:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:12:1.english: And showed its blemish - After slaughter, and it was found [to be] a permanent [blemish].

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:13:1.hebrew: דוקין - טייל"א, כמו "הנוטה כדוק שמים" (ישעיהו מ):
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:13:1.english: Cataracts - Teile [in Old French, meaning a film or cataract], as in: “Who stretches out the heavens like a curtain” (Isaiah 40:22).

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:14:1.hebrew: משתנין - מפני צער מיתה משתנה העין, ואף על גב דהשתא מיתחזי קבוע — אי הוה חזי ליה מחיים, הוה מיתחזי עובר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:14:1.english: They change - Due to the agony of death, the eye changes; and even though it now appears permanent, if [one] had seen it during [its] lifetime, it would have appeared transient.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:14:2.english: [Blemishes] on the body - For example, [if] its ear was split.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:14:3.hebrew: מפני המשתנין - כלומר, מפני דוקין שבעין שמשתנין — גזירה למומין שבגוף, אף על פי שאין משתנין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:14:3.english: Due to those that change - That is to say, on account of cataracts in the eye, which change, [there is] a decree regarding blemishes on the body, even though they do not change.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:1:1.hebrew: ואידך - דמפיק מובשרם יהיה לך וגו' — ההוא ודאי בחזה ושוק דתודה מישתעי, אלא שני ימים נפקא ליה מיהיה לך, דמשמע הויה אחרת לבר מזו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:1:1.english: And the other [one] - Who derives [it] from “And their flesh shall be yours, etc.”: That [verse] certainly speaks of the breast and thigh of a thanks offering; rather, [that it is eaten for] two days is derived by him from “shall be yours,” which implies another [period of] being beyond this one.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:3:1.hebrew: שלא מצינו בכל התורה כולה - שיתננו לכהן, אלא מרבויא דהאי יהיה לך נפקא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:3:1.english: As we have not found in the entire Torah - That [one] must give it to the priest; rather, it is derived from the amplification of this [phrase], “It shall be yours.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:4:1.hebrew: ואידך - דמפיק מיהיה לך שני ימים ולילה אחת — בכור בעל מום שניתן לכהן, מובשרם יהיה לך נפקא; לשון רבים משמע: אחד תם ואחד בעל מום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:4:1.english: And the other - [The one] who derives two days and one night from "it shall be yours" — [that] a blemished firstborn is given to a priest is derived from "and their flesh shall be yours"; a plural expression implies: one unblemished and one blemished.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:4:2.hebrew: ואידך ובשרם - לא משמע אלא תמימים, והא דנקט לשון רבים — דאבכורות דכולהו ישראל קאי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:4:2.english: And the other [held]: “And their flesh” - It implies only unblemished [firstborns]; and that which [the verse] used plural phrasing — [it is] because it refers to the firstborns of all of Israel.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:5:1.english: And after its year also thirty days - Even though the blemish developed well within its year.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:5:2.hebrew: כל י"ב חדש - עד שיהו לו שנים עשר חדש משנולד:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:5:2.english: The entire twelve months - Until it has twelve months from when it was born:

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:5:3.hebrew: היכא דנולד בו מום לאחר שנתו - רשאי לקיימו שלשים יום משנולד המום, דלאחר שנתו דמתני' ה"ק: ואם לאחר שנתו נולד המום, יקיימנו שלשים יום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:5:3.english: Where a blemish developed in it after its year - He is permitted to maintain it for thirty days from when the blemish developed, for [the phrase] “after its year” in the Mishnah means: And if the blemish developed after its year, he may maintain it for thirty days.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:6:1.english: In the present time - For an unblemished [animal] is not fit for anything.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:6:2.english: Until it is fit to be shown to a Sage - That no blemish developed on it after its [first] year.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:7:1.hebrew: אינו רשאי לקיימו אפילו יום אחד - וקס"ד אנולד בו מום בתוך שנתו קאי, וקתני: אבל מפני השבת אבידה לבעלים — דהיינו כהן, דשמא אם ביד ישראל הוי האי בכור לא משכח כהן למיתבי ליה, ואי שחיט ליה יסריח הבשר — אמרו רשאי לקיימו ל' יום, ואי לא משכח כהן, שוחטו ומולחו עד שימצא כהן. אלמא, ל' יום דקאמר, אנולד מום בתוך שנתו קאי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:7:1.english: He is not permitted to maintain it even for one day - And it entered our mind [to think that this] refers to [an animal] whose blemish developed within its [first] year, and it teaches: “However, due to returning a lost item to the owners” — that is, the priest, for perhaps if this firstborn is in the possession of an Israelite, he will not find a priest to give it to him, and if he slaughters it, the meat will spoil — [the Sages] said: He is permitted to maintain it [for] thirty days; and if he does not find a priest, he slaughters it and salts it until he finds a priest. Consequently, the thirty days that [the baraita] states refers to [a case where] a blemish developed within its year.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:8:1.hebrew: עדיין תיבעי - דברייתא גופה איכא לספוקא, דאיכא למימר: הא דקתני "לאחר שנתו אין רשאי לקיימו כו'", הכי קאמר: נולד בו לאחר שנתו, אין רשאי לקיימו כו', ועלה קאי "אבל מפני השבת אבידה כו'":
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:8:1.english: Still, let the dilemma be raised - For the baraita itself is subject to doubt, as it can be said: That which it teaches, "After its year he is not permitted to maintain it, etc.," this is what it means: [If a blemish] developed in it after its year, he is not permitted to maintain it, etc., and it is to this that "But due to returning a lost item, etc.," refers.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:8:2.hebrew: או דלמא קודם שנתו - כלומר, אם נולד מום קודם שנתו, נמי קאמר דלאחר שנתו שלשים יום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:8:2.english: Or perhaps before its year - That is to say, [perhaps] it is also saying that if a blemish developed before its year, after its year [he has] thirty days.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:9:1.hebrew: משלימין לו ט"ו אחר שנתו - אלמא, ל' יום דקתני מתני' — אנולד בו מום לאחר שנתו קאי. דאי נולד המום בתוך שנתו אפילו יום אחד, ליכא למימר דניתב ליה אחר שנתו שלשים יום, דלית ליה אלא השלמה, כדקתני בברייתא. ושמעינן מינה, דאי בתוך שנתו נולד המום, חדש או חדשים — רשאי לקיימו עד שנתו, דהא כתיב "שנה"; ואי לאחר שנה נולד מום, או קרוב לסיום שנתו — יהבינן ליה שלשים יום משנולד המום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:9:1.english: One completes for it fifteen [days] after its year - Evidently, the thirty days that the Mishnah teaches refers to [a case where] a blemish developed in it after its year. For if the blemish developed within its year, even [by] one day, it cannot be said that we should give him thirty days after its year, as he has only completion [of the thirty days], as taught in the baraita. And we learn from this that if the blemish developed within its year [with] a month or two months [remaining], he is permitted to keep it until [the end of] its year, for behold, it is written: "year"; and if a blemish developed after a year, or close to the conclusion of its year, we give him thirty days from when the blemish developed.

Rashi on Bekhorot 28a:9:2.english: One gives him thirty days - [This applies] if a blemish developed after its [first] year.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:13:1.hebrew: רבי מאיר סבר גזרינן מומין שבגוף כו' - ואומר רבי, דאע"ג דאמרינן בריש "אף על פי" (כתובות דף נז.) דהלכה כרבי מאיר בגזירותיו — הך דהכא, קרי ליה בסמוך "קנסא" דקא קניס ר' מאיר. ובשאלתות דרב אחאי פירש, דהלכה כמותו דוקא בגזירותיו ולא בקנסא; ופסקו דאין הלכה כמותו בההיא דמעוברת חברו ומינקת חברו, דקאמר רבי מאיר: "יוציא ולא יחזיר עולמית", וסוגיא דשמעתין בריש "החולץ" (יבמות דף לז.) דלא כר' מאיר. וכן סוגיא דשמעתין כרבי יהודה, דלרבי מאיר קנסינן בכולהו מפני המשתנין. ובסמוך דקאמר: "לימא תנן סתמא כרבי מאיר", הא משני: "דילמא בדוקין שבעין, ודברי הכל", וכן הוא אמת. ומתוך כך פוסק רבי דלא כרבי מאיר, דקניס בשטר שיש בו רבית, דאין גובה לא את הקרן ולא את הרבית (ב"מ דף עב.):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:13:1.english: "Rabbi Meir holds we issue a decree [regarding] blemishes on the body, etc." - And the Rabbi says that even though we say at the beginning of [the chapter] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 57a) that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir in his decrees, this [case] here, [the Gemara] nearby refers to it as a "penalty" that Rabbi Meir imposes. And in the She'iltot of Rav Achai it is explained that the halakha is like him specifically in his decrees, but not in a penalty. And they ruled that the halakha is not like him in that [case] of [one who marries] the pregnant [divorcee] of another or the nursing [mother] of another, where Rabbi Meir says: "He must divorce [her] and may never remarry [her]"; and the sugya of our Gemara at the beginning of [the chapter] HaCholetz (Yevamot 37a) is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir. And likewise, the sugya of our Gemara [here] is according to Rabbi Yehuda, for according to Rabbi Meir we penalize in all of them because of those [blemishes] that change. And nearby [on 28a], where [the Gemara] says: "Shall we say that we learned an anonymous [mishnah] according to Rabbi Meir?", behold, it answers: "Perhaps [it refers to] blemishes on the cornea, and it is agreed by all"; and so indeed is the truth. And based on this, the Rabbi rules not in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who penalizes in [the case of] a promissory note that contains interest, [holding] that he may collect neither the principal nor the interest (Bava Metzia 72a).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:1:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא בחזה ושוק של תודה - לר' עקיבא לית ליה כי הך סברא בסוף איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נז.), ומפרש דהתם פליגי בהימנו ודבר אחר, אי הוי היקש או לא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:1:1.english: "One would have thought [it is compared] to the breast and thigh of a thanks offering" - According to Rabbi Akiva, he does not hold of this reasoning at the end of Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 57a); and [the Gemara] explains that there they disagree over [whether a derivation from] "both it and another matter" is considered a juxtaposition or not.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:3:1.hebrew: שלא מצינו לו בכל התורה כולה - פי' בקונטרס: שיתננו לכהן אלא מריבויא. לפירושו, כן יכול לומר בכל דרשות! ומפרש ר"י דהכי קאמר: שלא מצינו לו בכל התורה כולה שיתננו, כולה כיוצא בזה; דחטאת ואשם שהם לכהן כשקריבין למזבח, אם הוממו — שהמזבח מפסיד חלקו, מפסיד גם לכהן; אבל בכור, אפילו בעל מום — דכהן הוא. וכן ההיא דפרק שתי מדות (מנחות דף צא:) גבי נסכים: "לכבש האחד" — זה אחד עשר של מעשר, שלא מצינו לו בכל התורה כולה שיהא טפל חמור מן העיקר; דהוה מצי למימר "אחד עשר של מעשר יוכיח", כדמשני אמותר מפסח. וכן בשבת בפ' אמר ר' עקיבא (שבת דף פג:): "זה היסטו של זב, שלא מצינו בכל התורה כולה דטומאה המסטת תטמא":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:3:1.english: “As we have not found it in the entire Torah” - The Kuntres explained: That one gives it to a priest, except [that we derive it] from an amplification [of the verse]. [However,] according to his explanation, one could say this about all derivations! And the Ri explains that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: We have not found in the entire Torah that one gives it [to a priest in] any case comparable to this. For [with regard to] a sin-offering and a guilt-offering, which belong to the priest when they are offered upon the altar, if they become blemished — since the altar loses its share, the priest also loses [his share]; but a firstborn, even [when] blemished, belongs to the priest. And similarly, that [passage] in the chapter [entitled] Shtei Middot (Menachot 91b) regarding libations: “[For] each lamb” — this is the eleventh [animal] of the [animal] tithe, as we have not found anywhere in the entire Torah that an ancillary [element] should be more stringent than the principal [element]; for [otherwise the Gemara] could have said: “Let the eleventh of the tithe prove [it],” as it answers with regard to the surplus of a Pesach offering. And similarly in Shabbat, in the chapter [entitled] Amar Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 83b): “This is the shifting of a zav, as we do not find anywhere in the entire Torah that a source of defilement that causes shifting transmits impurity.”

Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:4:1.hebrew: ואידך ובשרם דהני בכורות דכולהו ישראל קאמר - בסוף איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נז.) משני: רבי ישמעאל, "מבשרם" דהנך [בכורות] קאמר. משמע — רוצה לומר: דקאי אבכור שור וכשב ועז דכתיב לעיל מיניה, ושינויא אחרינא הוא. וא"ת: והא תנא לא דריש מידי מ"ובשרם" לשון רבים, ובסוגיא דהתם לעיל (שם דף נו:) דריש ר' יוסי הגלילי: "דמו" לא נאמר אלא "דמם", "חלבו" לא נאמר אלא "חלבם" — לימד על בכור ומעשר שטעונין מתן דמים ואמורין למזבח? וי"ל, דפלוגתא היא בר"פ בית שמאי בזבחים (דף לז.), ורבי ישמעאל נפקא ליה מ"דם זבחיך ישפך":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:4:1.english: “And the other [answers that] ‘and their flesh’ is said in reference to these firstborn of all of Israel” - At the end of [the chapter] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 57a), [the Gemara] answers that Rabbi Yishmael says [the verse's statement] “of their flesh” is said in reference to these [firstborn]. This implies it means to say that it refers to the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, and a goat that is written above it [in the verse]; and it is a different resolution. And if you say: But does this Tanna not derive anything from “and their flesh” [being in] the plural? Yet in the sugya there earlier (ibid. 56b), Rabbi Yosei HaGelili expounds: “His blood” was not stated, but rather “their blood”; “his fat” was not stated, but rather “their fat” — this taught concerning a firstborn and a tithe [offering] that they require the presentation of blood and sacrificial portions for the altar! And one can say that it is a dispute at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai in Zevachim (37a), and Rabbi Yishmael derives it from “And the blood of your offerings shall be poured.”

Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:6:1.hebrew: עד שלא נראה להראותו לחכם - פי' בקונטרס: שלא נפל בו מום. וקשה: מאי "רשאי לקיימו שתים ושלש שנים"? על כרחיך יקיימנו! ודוחק לפרש "רשאי" לשון חייב, כי ההיא דערכין (דף כח:): דמקדישין אותו הקדש עילוי, כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בקרבן זה לעשותו עולה, אע"פ שאינו רשאי — דפירושו כמו: אע"פ שאינו חייב. והוה מצינן לפרש דנקט "רשאי לקיימו", כלומר: ואין זקוק לכונסו לכיפה, אע"ג דשאר קדשים שהקדיש והחרים בזמן הזה אמרינן בפ"ק דע"ז (דף יג.): "בהמה תעקר", דנועל דלת בפניה והיא מתה מאיליה; אבל היה משמע דאם היה רוצה לכונסו לכיפה — כונסו, ומעשים בכל יום ששומרים אותם עד שיפול בהם מום. ונראה לפרש: "עד שלא נראה להראותו לחכם" — שלא נזדמן לו חכם אחר שנפל בו מום, שאין זקוק להוליכו במקום רחוק, למקום שהחכם שם:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:6:1.english: "Until it was not seen to show it to a sage" - Rashi explained in the commentary: That no blemish had fallen upon it. And this is difficult: What is [the meaning of] "he is permitted to maintain it for two or three years"? Perforce he must maintain it! And it is forced to explain "permitted" as an expression of obligation, like that [baraita] in Arakhin (28b): where they consecrate it with an assessment-consecration — how much a person is willing to give for this offering to make it an elevation-offering — "even though he is not permitted," whose meaning is like: "even though he is not obligated." And we could have explained that it formulated "he is permitted to maintain it," meaning: and he is not required to enclose it in a vaulted chamber, even though regarding other consecrated animals that one consecrated or declared devoted in the present time, we say in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (13a): "An animal shall be uprooted" — that is, one locks the door before it and it dies of its own accord; however, that would imply that if he wanted to enclose it in a vaulted chamber, he may enclose it, whereas it is daily practice that people keep them until a blemish falls upon them. And it appears [correct] to explain: "Until it was not seen to show it to a sage" — that a sage did not happen to be available to him after a blemish fell upon it, for he is not required to take it to a distant place, to the place where the sage is.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:7:1.hebrew: מפני השבת אבידה לבעלים - פי' בקונטרס: דהיינו כהן, דזימנין דלא משכח כהן למיתבא ליה, ואם ישחטנו מיד יסרח — לפיכך רשאי לקיימו שלשים יום אחר שנתו. ואומר רבי, דמיירי ביד כהן, וא"צ עכשיו לבשר, ונתנו לו חכמים זמן ל' יום; אבל ישראל לעולם ממתין עד שימצא כהן:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 28a:7:1.english: "Due to returning a lost item to the owners" - The Kuntres explained that this means the priest, for at times [an Israelite] does not find a priest to give it to him, and if he slaughters it immediately, [the meat] will spoil; therefore, he is permitted to maintain it for thirty days after its year. And the Rabbi says that [the baraita] is dealing with [a firstborn that is] in the possession of a priest, and he does not need meat now, so the Sages gave him a period of thirty days; but an Israelite always waits until he finds a priest.
